svg.title: Connection budget of the Magento database tier: pods times PHP-FPM workers against max_connections
svg.desc: Diagram of how many connections the Pocket Coffee cluster can open to the RDS instance pocketcoffee-prod. On the left, the web Deployment at its autoscaling maximum of eight pods with twenty PHP-FPM workers each, which is one hundred and sixty workers and, because Magento opens one connection per PHP process, one hundred and sixty connections. Below it the admin Deployment with two pods of ten workers, the cron pod with about twelve processes, the queue consumers at their maximum of ten, the reindex Job with five and the release Job with one, plus about ten for monitoring and people. A rolling update adds a surge of old and new pods together, here forty-five more. These numbers are examples. On the right, a horizontal bar represents max_connections of the instance, for example 600: the web pods fill twenty-seven percent of it, admin, background work and the surge add up to 263 connections in total, and the remaining 337 are headroom that must stay free for failover reconnects, slow queries and people running mysql by hand. The rule printed at the bottom is that the sum of the worst cases must stay below max_connections, and that lowering pm.max_children, a bigger instance class or RDS Proxy are the three ways to restore the budget.
svg.text: Connection math: worst case against max_connections
Example numbers for pocketcoffee-prod; read your own max_connections and measure Max_used_connections
pocketcoffee-web at the HPA maximum
8 pods x pm.max_children 20 = 160 PHP-FPM workers
Each busy worker: 1 connection (the default one)
No split checkout or sales connection any more
worst case 160 x 1 = 160
Everything else that holds a connection
pocketcoffee-admin: 2 pods x 10 workers = 20
pocketcoffee-cron: cron:run and its group processes, about 12
consumers: 3 Deployments at maximum 4 + 4 + 2 = 10
reindex Job with MAGE_INDEXER_THREADS_COUNT=4: 5
migrate Job 1, health probes, exporter, people: about 11
fixed and admin: about 58
rolling update: old and new pods together, here +45
RDS instance: max_connections = 600 (example)
web 160
headroom 337
263 of 600 in the worst case. The headroom is not waste:
- a failover, when every pod reconnects at once
- slow queries that keep connections busy longer
- a second reindex Job or a manual setup:upgrade
- people running mysql by hand
If the budget cannot be met: lower pm.max_children or the HPA
maximum, use a larger instance class, or put RDS Proxy in front
of the web pods (clients keep 160, the database sees fewer).
Rule
(max pods x pm.max_children) + consumers + cron + Jobs + a rolling-update surge + a failover margin must stay below max_connections
Magento opens one connection per PHP process; the Mage-OS and Adobe 2.4.9 adapter reconnects up to 10 times after error 2006, 2013 or 4031.
